topic.readerProblem: A founder, marketer or agency lead wants ChatGPT to name and link their brand when buyers ask for recommendations, and needs to know how ChatGPT search finds sources, what actually works, what is hype, and how to check the result.
topic.connection: AEOeye's free audit asks ChatGPT unbranded buyer questions live and shows whether the brand is named; this guide explains the retrieval path behind those answers, uses AEOeye's own crawler access study and audit records, and tells the reader what to change when the brand is missing.

assessment: The page answers one question, how to get ChatGPT to recommend and cite a brand, by describing the ChatGPT search path as OpenAI documents it (help-center and crawler pages, October 2026), separating mentions from citations, and giving an ordered playbook (crawler and firewall access, raw HTML, Bing and Google indexing, answer pages, third-party corroboration, shopping feeds) plus a repeated-prompt measurement protocol. It rests on OpenAI's own documentation, two arXiv papers, a 100-query Bing-overlap test, a Vercel crawler analysis, and AEOeye's crawler access study (384 sites) and audit records (161 ChatGPT answers, with their caveats). It deliberately does not claim a ranking formula, a timeline, that Bing alone feeds ChatGPT, or that llms.txt or schema moves citations, and it drops the merged pages' unverified vendor statistics and their 'no paid placement' line, which ChatGPT ads (Free and Go plans) have made incomplete.

sources.supports: Defines generative engine optimization, also called answer engine optimization, as improving visibility in responses generated by AI systems.

ChatGPT may search automatically; it rewrites questions into one or more targeted queries and may send follow-ups; responses may include citations and a Sources list; results and citations can be incomplete, outdated or incorrect and users are told to check when a source was published or updated; search sometimes partners with other providers (Microsoft and Shopify privacy policies linked); approximate location is used for local results; sites should allow OAI-SearchBot and OpenAI's published IP addresses.
Training data includes publicly available internet content; there is an inherent element of randomness, so the same question may yield different answers.

OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; opted-out sites are not shown in answers; robots.txt changes take about 24 hours; OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot settings are independent; OpenAI publishes IP ranges.

February 2025 test: 100 queries, 500-plus citations; 87% of citations matched Bing's top organic results versus a 56% match with Google; the authors flag query simplification, a bias toward 'best' and 'top' queries and a small sample.

September 2025 preprint: 1,000 consumer ranking prompts on search-enabled engines including gpt-4o-search-preview via API; in the U.S. software category AI search returned 72.7% earned, 26.7% brand and negligible social sources versus 45.4% earned and 43.7% brand for Google.
December 2024 analysis of Vercel's network: none of the major AI crawlers, including OpenAI's, render JavaScript; recommends server-side rendering for critical content.
IndexNow lets site owners notify participating search engines of content changes and lists Microsoft Bing among its supporters.
GEO paper accepted to KDD 2024: generative engine optimization can boost visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40%, on the GEO-bench benchmark.

Full text: statistics, quotation and cite-sources methods performed best; keyword stuffing offered little to no improvement; main evaluation used a gpt-3.5-turbo engine with top five fetched sources and was also run on Perplexity.ai.
Product results are selected by ChatGPT and are not ads; Shopify merchants are integrated through Shopify Catalog; other merchants can apply to send a direct product feed.
Ads may appear for Free and Go users below a response, labeled as sponsored; OpenAI says ads do not influence ChatGPT's answers; testing started in the U.S. on 9 February 2026.
August 2024 final rule bans fake or false reviews and testimonials, explicitly including AI-generated fake reviews, and lets the FTC seek civil penalties against knowing violators.

January 2026 study (600 volunteers, 2,961 runs across ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI): under a 1-in-100 chance that two responses list the same brands, about 1 in 1,000 for the same order; visibility percentage across many runs is a reasonable metric.
With Memory enabled ChatGPT may use relevant details to formulate a search query; temporary chats can be started as Unpersonalized and do not create or update memories.

Publishers who allow OAI-SearchBot can track ChatGPT referral traffic because ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral URLs; blocking OAI-SearchBot is what keeps content out of summaries and snippets.

Google does not prohibit AI-generated content but warns that generating many pages without adding value may violate its scaled content abuse policy and tells publishers to fact-check AI output; page shows last updated 1 October 2026.
